html:
The British zone was the part of defeated Germany that Britain occupied from 1945 to 1949, in the northwest: the Ruhr industrial region, Hamburg, Lower Saxony and Schleswig-Holstein.

It was the most industrial and the most crowded zone, and also the hungriest. Its cities had been bombed flat, and refugees from the east poured in. Britain, nearly bankrupt itself, had to import food to keep people alive. The British reorganised the old Prussian provinces into new states, among them North Rhine-Westphalia and Lower Saxony, and tried to break up the coal and steel combines of the Ruhr.

To share the cost, Britain merged its zone economically with the American one in 1947 into the "Bizone". The Marshall Plan and the currency reform of 1948 started recovery, and during the Berlin Blockade British planes flew supplies into the city. In 1949 the zone became part of West Germany, within the larger occupation regime of Allied-occupied Germany.
sum: The British zone was the part of defeated Germany that Britain occupied from 1945 to 1949, in the northwest: the Ruhr industrial region, Hamburg, Lower Saxony and Schleswig-Holstein.
